answer: Salvage crews used to photocopy one permit and claim every wreck on the shelf. A harbor now issues a single relic ticket per watch: the diver posts 47 units, picks a numbered cage on the ocean floor, and pre-commits C=sha256(cage_no||watch_id||pubkey||sonar_bin) before the timing pulse from the bell buoy. Five dock clerks unseal C and replay the hydrophone roll; the stake returns after 11 hours only if that cage_no is unique. If two keys share one cage or one pulse window, both stakes burn and the cage is struck, so minting extra identities costs more than any wreck they could lift.
